The Retirement Standard rides five registered families: retirement:{state}:v1 (self-emitted lifecycle row; the retired row names the custodian key), preserve_request:v1 (the signed ask naming preserve_until and carrying the best-practice copy rule), preserve_response:v1 (the operator's accepted/declined), archive_release:{basis}:v1 (WA-emitted; the one row that opens a seal; a key grant on a sealed archive cites it), lawful_order:release:v1 (the steward's record of an order to release)

The custodian key that signs custody rows after retirement is named in the agent's final retirement:retired:v1 row and admitted because that row names it (the lineage-witness rule), never by a delegates_to; no term applies; it holds no seal key

A lawful order to destroy sealed retirement material is a takedown_notice:court_order:v1 executed as the one tombstone by digest with the CC 4.5.3 purge guarantees; a person's deletion inside the sealed record is the same tombstone on the record's plane; no lawful_order:destroy and no record_tombstone family exists
A latched constitutional halt is not a leg of the trust chain (T3) and moves no T8 state; the agent's act gate is the only gate that reads the latch; reporting its state as a signal is not a gate

Erasure at the subject's request: an ordinary row by the subject's withdraws (2.4.1.1 rule 2, or rule 3 with the node as proxy); an adverse row (capacity, detection, licensure, revocation) only by its producer under rule 1 or refused with reason under Art. 17(3), never by a subject-authority path (formal/withdraws_admission, controller-only closes); the replicated fact is the tombstone by digest per plane; no node-local purge basis; a hard case recording an erasure names no subject

The subject of the target attestation, or a review-holder for the action's community, is admitted to file reconsideration:{grounds} against a prior action; the ruling stays with review-holders; no immediate-removal basis from any claimant

The agent protects itself under resource pressure by a published ladder, throttle (the loop slows and lifts), shed (refused at intake before credit, and lifts), drain (requests an orderly shutdown only); runtime self-protection is not a decision the agent made and borrows none of its decision verbs (plain rule 10b)
The agent's optional rest states (dream, play, solitude) are enabled by default and are presented to the runtime and operator, never imposed as duties (the self-improvement options of 1.13.2)
Change or drift in the agent's behavioural guidance is measured against its charter; above the published threshold the identity variance monitor requests a Wise Authority review (G21; plain rule 5e)
Only a ROOT or AUTHORITY principal may force a shutdown over the agent's objection (G16); the force path is to be confirmed and the row published on its staging ticket

The signed object is attestation_envelope alone (JCS, RFC 8785): seven columns mirrored inside the bytes under row (closed; a missing mirror is refused envelope_member_missing, a diverging column typed_diverges_from_envelope); asserted_at/expires_at signed twins; the row's own signature is the attester's over those bytes (Ed25519; ML-DSA-65 over bytes||ed25519_sig, strict at the federation tier); cosigners ride additional_scrubs beside the row over the same bytes; original_content_hash recomputed at ingest

Byte vectors for the signed object: two test identities with CC 2.6.8 key_ids; minimal scores, explicit-default twin, subject-and-scope, cosigned, withdraws, at-cap and cap-plus-one recipes, six refusal cases; JCS bytes, original_content_hash and the Ed25519 half recomputed in CI (tools/build_cc_signed_object.py --self-test); ML-DSA-65 produced and verified by ciris-crypto at the verify pin

A roster key other than the genesis key is named <fedID>-<own fingerprint> (the whole fedID as the 2.6.8 label); a device-derived id and a bare-label id are refused; a consumer never treats a roster key id as a different identity
Any live roster key signs as the fedID for every owner act; an owner/steward gate accepts a live roster key of the same fedID at the row's asserted_at, not only the key named on the binding

An addition or eviction is a proposal by a live roster key landing by strict majority at once or after W_self = 86400 s with no majority objection (eviction: target silent all window); unilateral at one key; there is no any-occurrence-evicts-at-once door
A roster key lives on one node and a node holds at most one roster key of a self; the node's own key is a different key
The ruled two-path policy closes at three keys (one stolen; two lost) and four (one stolen, one lost); two keys: one lost closes, one stolen stalls with safety held; unilateral fails in two steps
Known-abuse scanning happens only where content is published to everyone or posted into a public room; private scopes are never scanned (model witness: no scan reaches a self/family/community blob)
A root can only tell a node to share less: every root act narrows the allow set and none widens it; a restriction needs a subscribed root
No act of a root removes a community; withdrawal is node by node and root by root (the hand that could remove predators removes dissidents)

Leaving a root is one act by the node's owner (the acceptance edge deleted), which lifts the root's duties and the reach of every later halt and leaves the record standing; a halt latched before the cut keeps its reach until it lapses or is resumed
Every binding over a participant is revocable by the party that made it: consent requires revocability and no finding removes it

The Retirement Standard as a machine: the seven states advance in order and only forward; cancellation only before frozen; secrets destroyed before hand-over; custody rows only by the custodian the retired row names; the seal opens by one archive_release row (WA approval or recorded lawful order); a walk-away is always enabled and keeps the record; the ladder completes with one postponement per proposal; must-fail twins for each

The consent plane as a machine: a revocation is a boundary and nothing is captured after it until a fresh grant; a revocation wins a tie; a stranger's grant moves nothing; the owner, the node and the subject can always recant; backdating is bounded by W and a withdrawn signer keeps at most W of authority; an empty scope matches nothing; decay starts only after revocation or expiry and runs forward to complete; expired is substrate-emitted; replication needs a directed grant (3.3.7); twins for the no-boundary, literal-signer and no-W readings fail

The membership ceremony as a machine: an acceptance binds to exactly one live proposal by proposal_hash and a proposal seats at most once; a decline is terminal; no key is seated on rows it alone signed; every widening and removal that lands meets the group's consensus_protocol on the roster at the row's instant; one coerced key never removes an honest member under unanimous, majority or quorum (founder_only is the stated bound); a member can always resign; a departed member is re-seated only by a new proposal; every member consented; no proposal outlives its window; a held change resolves; four protocols close, eight twins fail as named

The generalized two-path policy (enact, cancel, floor, window, irreversible) over a standing set: a coerced minority below cancel never blocks a floored honest change; an active honest set at cancel stops every adversarial change; with a floor above one voter no change lands on a single approval however many voters are silent; below the floor nothing lands; the irreversible wait its window; honest proposals resolve — seven instances close, the no-floor twin fails by one voice landing over four silent voters

A two-path policy is admissible only inside the corridor: neither the rigidity pole (one voice cancels, or unanimity) nor the chaos pole (one voice enacts, nothing cancels, or one voice lands by silence); cancel ≤ enact, floor ≤ enact, enact at least a strict majority, window at its sensitivity floor; a zero floor is the chaos pole at every size and every corridor policy floors at two voices or more; the floor and the cancel fraction scale with the expected-active base, not the standing roster, above the small-community size

The two-path policy is published as data: one table of five numbers per door (enact, cancel, floor, window, irreversible) over a named standing set and base, checked against the corridor at build, with a decision function, vectors mapping (policy, base, approvals, objections, elapsed) to a verdict, and one TLC instance per two-path row; the floor never lands before the window; no vector lands on one voice at base > 2

The community_trust capture grant may be authored by the node's owner: attester a live roster key of the owner's fedID at asserted_at, attested the node, subject_key_ids the node, the owner-at-asserted_at and the agent key; each may withdraw, the attester alone recants; the node-authored form stays valid
An unowned node originates exactly one kind of message, a device-join request on the pairing plane under its receiver order, and serves and asserts nothing else until bound
The owner's one approval signs two rows each standing alone, the owner-binding and the device occurrence, binding admitted first, applied by the joining node before it links
The matching code the owner compares is derived by the owner's own node from the request (requester key and challenge) and is never supplied by the requester

A lost, stolen or unfit custodian key is replaced by one cosigned retirement:custodian_minted:v1 row from the operator holding the record and the Wise Authority; the old key's custody rows before that instant stay valid

A planned retirement opens an objection window on its decided row in which the agent may object or ask to postpone, one postponement per proposal, the decider then decides; emergency and the halt take none of it

A node holding a serve seat in an infrastructure community has a live federation-scoped owner-binding while it holds the seat, so a named human answers for it; evaluated live (a later binding satisfies, a withdrawn one does not); without one the node does not serve under the seat, refused serve_seat_owner_unannounced; nothing in genesis carries the binding

WholenessWitness and member_commitment leaf lists are sorted AND deduplicated; a list with a repeated leaf is refused before hashing, so {a,b,c} and {a,b,c,c} cannot both be presented and odd-node duplication is moot; descend refuses a duplicate source id

Under the per-link hybrid seal an unowned joining device is never anonymous: its self-signed node key is bound into the handshake, equals the join request's signer and the matching code's input, the responder is the owner's announced node, and the link carries only the pairing plane
Proof of possession at key registration and device pairing verifies the key_id fingerprint against the public key; a record claiming another key's id is refused

A legacy framed occurrence revocation replicates as identity:occurrence_revocation:v1, minted by persist from the verified signed object (attester the revoker, byte-exact re-derivation); admitted for node and agent occurrences, and for a user self only when cosigned by a strict majority of the current live roster, so no carrier bypasses the two-path door

The genesis bundle (version 4) carries the seated serve nodes' signed transport_destination rows with their transit pairs in serve_transport_destinations, inside the authorization digest, verified closed at bundle verification and seeded Rooted at first open; a seated serve node keeps the bundle's pair valid until a re-minted bundle has propagated (a rotation that would retire the pinned pair first is refused at the rotation door)
For an offline or LAN-only pairing the owner's pairing payload carries the owner node's transit pair, pinned for that one pairing link only and never stored Rooted, under the key-bound rules

A seated serve node's transport destination and transit pair are re-bound by the accord holders' cosigned transport:canonical_rebind:v1 row at the charter's threshold, landing Rooted and superseding the bundle-seeded binding; below threshold refused; a unilateral early rotation refused at the node's rotation door

A dialler holding no transit pair for the dialled node sends a route request as its first frame; the responder answers with its own hybrid-signed transport_destination row, plus its own key:record:v1 row when the dialler says it holds none, and nothing else; the dialler verifies it under the authenticated-pair rule before the handshake; rate-limited by the receiver order, nothing served before the seal, any other first frame dropped; the pairing pin is the failover

An initiator seals only to a transit pair authenticated to the identity it means to reach (that identity's own hybrid-signed binding from any source, a Rooted binding, or a pairing pin); a bare announce supplies nothing; Rooted governs what is served, not whether two keys may speak; a node relays every held signed route row with a pair, so two peers with any mutual peer seal and root with no canonical

observation:access_assumption:v1 is a first-person row by a witness about the view it scored through (grants via consent_basis, trace_level, occurrence_key_ids, window, channel_classes); subject_key_ids non-empty naming the observed agent; never emitted by the subject; every cited grant live at asserted_at

An identity_occurrence row names the build it runs (build_manifest_hash, build_manifest_ref to a provenance:build_manifest row that is Rooted at the receiver and whose manifest hash matches); a row about a running occurrence resolves its version through the roster, never from a producer-asserted string

The capacity row's envelope-extra members (consent_basis, n_eff_pr, n_eff_h, sample_size, feature_dim, sample_size_gate, target_n_eff, min_feature_dim, n_eff_floor, window) have CC 2.1 rows with their shapes as CIRISServer emits them, validated at the capacity:* gate

Shaping is a per-link property negotiated in the CTKX handshake (budget class, lower offer wins, node-wide cap); both directions shaped or the link declined; constant MDU-sized sealed frames on a per-link Poisson timer with cover dominance real ≤ ρ over W; audio/video never shaped; off by default; link setup and the existence of unshaped links stay observable

Using the Anonymous Tier is the publisher's opt-in; every node relays onion traffic for others by default; a non-serve node MAY opt out by the onion_relay opt_out marker plus withdrawing its hop key, a serve node MAY NOT (seat_opted_out, seat_without_hop_key); phone-class nodes relay by default only on Wi-Fi while charging, user-overridable; the tier's first scope is federation-scope publication

A relaying node (every serve node) carries a static X-Wing onion hop key onion_hop_pubkeys {ml_kem_768_base64, x25519_base64} on its hybrid-signed transport_destination binding (envelope-only; reuse refused onion_hop_x25519_reuse / onion_hop_ml_kem_768_reuse), rotatable by supersedes, in-row separated from the transit pair and every other key on the row; no valid hop key means the node cannot relay onion traffic

An onion packet is fixed-length and layered, each layer encapsulated to the hop's X-Wing key (post-quantum at every hop); a route has exactly three hops, one per layer; layers are assigned from serve seats deterministically over the fold; packets ride as bodies of shaped frames; hop keys, layers and rendezvous indexes rotate on global clocks

rendezvous:route:v1 is a federation-scope row self-signed by a fresh hybrid rendezvous key per hour (identity_type rendezvous, key record inline, no standing), carrying the receiver's three-hop reply header and its layer-3 mailbox seat (MUST be a serve seat; one seat per mailbox); a rendezvous key offered to the key plane as an identity is refused federation_rendezvous_key_not_an_identity; one route per period reused, each period superseding the last, purgeable after valid_until

A relay for a period is a node whose live, announced transport_destination row carries a valid hop key and no opt-out marker, owner-bound under a bundle root, with shaped layer links at use; per rendezvous period the relays are sorted by H(key_id || period), seats first, and dealt round-robin across three layers; unconferred relays per layer are capped at ceil(c x conferred relays), a conferred relay being a serve seat or an infra:relay role-holder, c default 2; a layer under three members makes the tier unavailable that period; all a pure function of the fold; availability at a node additionally needs three answering relays per layer within the period (a per-node liveness measure)

The durability tier: an owner marks an item durable on publish (family- or community-scoped) with a target holder count; the blob swarm replicates its encrypted chunks to that count across the live cohort, rarest chunk first; repair runs when the holonomic view shows holders falling toward the floor; recovery is pulling the chunks from any holder and decrypting with the recovered cohort key; nodes never encode stored content
An item un-marked or withdrawn descends: holders drop to normal retention, then none; no node is made to hold more by the descent of another

Every node keeps an inventory: what it holds (a count and a hybrid-signed Merkle root per scope and plane) and how deeply each item is held (holders per item, own share, gap to target); an absent or lapsed claim is unknown, never none; inventories are pure folds over signed inputs and disagreement is detected by comparing witness roots; what the mesh holds is learned only through the census; measurement changes behaviour only through mesh_config, relieve-never-expand

The mesh census: one fixed-size secret-shared one-hot return per rooted node per period, each share to a different aggregator with a linear validity proof; composite = partial_a + partial_b with mass_total = source_count and n_eff = source_count; k = 10 owners per published cell, levels never deltas, values rounded to a grid; no return carries any Anonymous Tier field and onion users are never counted; the 4.5.13 base is the member-only expected-active count over four periods under a ratchet (at most a tenth per period, never below the floor, frozen on a fall over a third); governance acts stay identified, a community may hold a secret poll (ballot secrecy claimed, coercion resistance not)

The seven census families (census:share/partial/composite:{class}:v1, census:member:share:v1, census:member:partial:v1, census:expected_active:v1, ballot:tally:{poll_id}:v1) and the addressed placement: a row whose signed for_key_id names one recipient is held by author and recipient only and refused elsewhere federation_addressed_not_recipient; the twenty census and ballot door tokens as registered, aggregation_meta_dominated and aggregation_meta_multiplicity reused; an aggregator deletes a share once summed and holds none past the period

One voice never decides who is in a room: a community record above the family naming founder_only is refused federation_community_consensus_protocol_violation; open:self_admit is the open protocol of a public group (self-signed admission) and there the two-voice floor and the roster window attach to removal

The census and the secret poll as modelled: a colluding aggregator's view is independent of every other owner's accepted report, the partials sum to the accepted reports, every accepted report is one-hot and counted once per owner (n_eff = source_count), no cell publishes under k owners or with one owner over half the mass, a member's cell is emitted at the fixed size whether or not a poll is open, the base falls at most a tenth per period and never below its floor and holds while frozen, and a poll passes only against the base of its period; nine instances close, eight twins fail where named, counting facts for any modulus in Lean

The Wise Authority board row on the declared-asymmetry register names its bound and its exit from Annex B (staggered three-year terms with a two-term maximum, 8.8.2 §2; removal by a two-thirds vote, §9), which is an operational target and not a wire object; the asymmetry stays declared, not resolved, until the board's roster and its removals are signed rows or the privilege is ratified entrenched

The layer deal is deterministic over the fold, an adversary holding no conferred relay holds at most c/(1+c) of any layer, a route through the tier is never more exposed than publishing without it, and a layer under three is reported unavailable rather than dealt thin; proved at four checked sizes and by counting for any N

An agent's deferral is deferral:request:v1 (occurrence key, cell audience, agent inactive until answered; re-routed to the live quorum on window expiry) and a Wise Authority's answer is deferral:response:{approved|rejected}:v1 signed by the WA's own key, referencing the request; not a wa_adjudication finding

An applied identity amendment is identity_amendment:v1 by the agent's occurrence key about its identity key, carrying amendment_digest and authorized_by, admitted only when the cited deferral:response is admitted, approved, about this agent and signed by a key seated as a Wise Authority at its asserted_at (else identity_amendment_unauthorized); the build is read from the occurrence row
wa_adjudication:{state} is closed to abandonment, seizure and successor, each a WA-quorum finding over the full seated roster

What crosses before Rooted: on a sealed link to an un-Rooted peer the bootstrap kinds, the allegiance facts, the pairing plane, rows addressed to the peer and every row a bounded cohort delivers to the peer as its member cross; Rooted gates what the node serves to a third party (federation-tier rows, self-authored rows about others)

The 2-holder cap binds the whole-object fetch; a chunked object is fetched chunk by chunk under the same cap at chunk granularity (no chunk from more than 2 holders in parallel); per-holder in-flight depth is the implementer's; ContentMiss downweight per holder on either path

A node offers an identity:occurrence:v1 row only when it would relay the attester's key to that peer (owner-binding announced at federation scope, per node); an agent identity's attester meets the same test through its steward binding and announced owner-binding, no special case
